title: Intelligence Measurement: Stanford-Binet-5, Raven's, Culture Fair, Naglieri, Bhatia
summary: Major intelligence tests; Stanford-Binet Intelligence Scale-5; Raven's Progressive Matrices; Culture Fair Intelligence Test; Naglieri Non-Verbal; Bhatia Battery; subtests and scales.
objectives: Describe Culture Fair Intelligence Test purpose.
revision: Intelligence tests: Stanford-Binet-5 (five factors), Raven's (non-verbal), Culture Fair (bias-reduced), Naglieri, Bhatia. IQ: mean 100, SD 15.
confusions: Believing IQ = 100/SD 15 applies to all tests.

notes.t: Stanford-Binet-5 measures five cognitive factors: fluid reasoning, knowledge, quantitative reasoning, visual-spatial processing and working memory. Provides Full Scale IQ and factor index scores.
A non-verbal, culture-reduced test of abstract reasoning using visual pattern completion. Suitable for diverse populations and those with language difficulties.
Designed to minimise cultural and language bias. Uses non-verbal items such as series completion, classification, matrices and conditions.

r: Performance intelligence test developed in India

notes.t: IQ scores are typically distributed with mean = 100 and SD = 15. Classification: 130+ = very superior, 120–129 = superior, 110–119 = high average, 90–109 = average, 80–89 = low average, 70–79 = borderline, below 70 = extremely low.
UGC NET frequently asks about specific intelligence tests and their features. Stanford-Binet-5 = five factors; Raven's = non-verbal culture-reduced.
